notes: Baseline integration of the symmetric five-sensor geometry with a proportional steering law, sized for about 1.5 m/s. Geometry is unchanged from the Builder's proposal. Gains are first-principles estimates, not tuned values. Adds control_effort and controller_errors to the requested measurements to help diagnose gain problems and runtime faults.
rationale: Iteration 0 has no Integration Race Data and no earlier outcomes, so this controller is a first-principles baseline for the supplied geometry, not a tuned one. The geometry is kept exactly as the Builder supplied it (five sensors at x = -0.02 to 0.02 m, y = 0.04 m, 12 mm footprints, 0.12 m track, 0.03 m wheels, 0.6 kg). Sensor x is positive to the left and positive weights steer left, so each weight is set proportional to its sensor's x position: [-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1]. A reading on the left sensors pushes the signal positive, steering the robot back toward the tape. With readings in [0, 1], the signal stays within about ±1. kp = 3 gives turn up to about ±3, which is roughly ±1050 PWM between the wheels, a firm but not saturating response for the expected bends. ki = 0.1 is kept small because the integral can only reach ±2, and it is there mainly to remove steady bias from the fixed left/right motor mismatch. kd = 0.1 damps overshoot from the 0.04 m lookahead without amplifying sensor noise much. base_speed = 1.8 gives PWM base of about 3685, which should give the 1.5 m/s average needed to finish inside 3 s while keeping some margin for slowdowns on the slalom. line_loss = 'last_direction' lets the robot keep turning the way it was going when the tape drops out, which suits the bends better than a fixed search. I expect this to complete the development tracks with few line-loss events, and I have no measured result yet to support that. The race will show whether kp or base_speed is the limit.
